A hyper-realistic, life size wooden Japanese doll by artist Hananuma Masakichi. San Francisco. c. 1900

Hananuma Masakichi (1832-1895) was a Japanese sculptor. Believing that he was dying from tuberculosis, Hananuma sculpted a life size statue of himself as a gift to the woman he loved, which was completed in 1885. The artist himself died 10 years later, in poverty aged 63.

The statue is renowned for being nearly identical in appearance to its creator. Made of between 2000 and 5000 wooden strips, it is connected only by dovetail joints, glue and wooden pegs. No joint is visible on the statue, and it is lacquered to show every detail of Hananuma, including muscle, bone and vein. The artist also manufactured anatomically correct glass eyeballs for the statue. Finally, individual holes were drilled in the statue to represent the pores of the skin, and the corresponding hair inserted.

The statue was purchased by Robert Ripley (of Believe it or Not fame) in 1934 and was reportedly his favorite of all the pieces he owned.
